--- earlier in this thread, from the person who asked (oldest first) ---

take Escher woodcut circle limit III and make it an interactive explorer. Let the user pick a row of fish to “swim” or translate n The direction of their nose and let the other fish follow as they must to preserve tiling. Effectively, use tiling to play with a Poincaré disk hyperbolic

Reasonable start. I think the interlocking is critical, you should make a geometric model and run the fish as tesselating polygons. Then the Poincaré conformal map will be sensible, and the interlocking falls out ~for free

Yes but. They have to look like fish! And they have to extend endlessly. So you’re always generating some radius around center with a mathematical description of the tiling. As long as you keep the geometry periodic it’s gonna be fiiine. I know drawing is a challenge so why dont you do hex tiling

Still not infinite. It HAS to be infinite tilings
